user: A vendor in Erode buys 12 kg of dried chilli at 95 rupees per kg and 8 kg at 70 rupees per kg. What average price per kg does she pay?

user: A Balasore excursion has 55 people in three vehicles. The first two vehicles take 18 people each. The third has 23 seats. How many seats remain free in it?

user: At a Jalna site, a 600-litre tank holds 160 litres. A pump adds 35 litres a minute for eight minutes. Workers use 70 litres. How many more litres will fill the tank?

user: A Udupi bakery has six days to prepare 108 gift boxes. The first three days produce 18 boxes apiece and the fourth produces 16. How many per day are needed on the last two days for an even finish?

user: Two schools in Nanded have waiting lists of 34 and 42 pupils for a science show. The theatre holds 190, but 18 seats are reserved for staff and 97 pupils already have tickets. The first school gets 60% of the seats available to the waiting lists. The second school gets all seats the first school does not use. How many pupils from each list still need seats?
think:
Pupil capacity is 190 - 18 = 172 seats.
The waiting lists can use 172 - 97 = 75 seats.
The planned allocation for the first school is 75 × 60 / 100 = 45 seats.
The first school uses only 34, so it gives back 45 - 34 = 11 seats.
The second school can use 75 - 45 + 11 = 41 seats.
The remaining demand is 34 - 34 = 0 at the first school and 42 - 41 = 1 at the second.
answer: No pupils remain on the first list, and 1 pupil remains on the second.

user: On a Konkan route, Ravi plans three stretches of 45, 60 and 30 km. His actual second stretch is 12 km longer. He travels at a constant 42 km per hour over the first two stretches together and at 30 km per hour over the last. He stops for 20 minutes and has 4 hours for the trip. How much time does he have left at the end?
think:
The changed second stretch measures 60 + 12 = 72 km.
The initial two stretches cover 45 + 72 = 117 km.
Those stretches take 117 / 42 × 60 = 1170 / 7 minutes.
The final stretch lasts 30 / 30 × 60 = 60 minutes.
With the stop the trip takes 1170 / 7 + 60 + 20 = 1730 / 7 minutes.
The planned time is 4 × 60 = 240 minutes.
Time left is 240 - 1730 / 7 = -50 / 7 minutes, so he exceeds his allowance.
answer: Ravi finishes 7 and 1/7 minutes over the time allowance.

user: A co-operative in Palanpur delivers 250 kg of grain. Its contract pays 36 rupees per kg for up to 180 kg and 30 per kg for the excess. The buyer rejects 10 kg before pricing. Transport costs 650 rupees. Separately, a member prepays a quarter of that transport cost, so the co-operative pays only the rest. What amount remains from the sale after the co-operative's own transport expense?
think:
The buyer accepts 250 - 10 = 240 kg.
The first price band brings 180 × 36 = 6480 rupees.
The second band applies to 240 - 180 = 60 kg.
This adds 60 × 30 = 1800 rupees.
The member covers 650 / 4 = 162.5 rupees of transport.
The co-operative pays 650 - 162.5 = 487.5 rupees for transport.
The proceeds remaining are 6480 + 1800 - 487.5 = 7792.5 rupees.
answer: The co-operative retains 7792 rupees and 50 paise.

user: A music group in Mysuru starts with 120 drum straps and 98 buckles. It tests 20 straps and finds that all 20 are unusable. Ten buckles go to another class. Four straps and four buckles are used in each finished set. The sets are sold for 160 rupees each, and the group must pay 210 rupees stall rent and 8 rupees for packaging every set. The straps can supply 100 / 4 = 25 sets.

Sales bring in 22 × 160 = 3520 rupees.
Packaging and rent together cost 22 × 8 + 210 = 386 rupees.
After those charges, 3520 - 386 = 3134 rupees remain.

user: A Madurai stage crew has 16 metres of black fabric and 14 metres of blue fabric. The black fabric can cover 1400 / 50 = 28 panels.
The blue fabric can cover 1320 / 55 = 24 panels, so only 24 are made.
The sale leaves 24 - 6 = 18 for the stage crew.
Dividing among three entrances gives 18 / 3 = 6 each.

user: In Guwahati, a community group prepares a 26 m by 16 m courtyard for a food fair. A separate 5 m by 4 m platform and a 6 m by 6 m play area remain bare. Covering the rest takes one roll per 10 square metres. It wants 10% more coverage than the area calls for and already has four full rolls. How many whole rolls should it buy?
think:
The courtyard covers 26 × 16 = 416 square metres.
The platform takes 5 × 4 = 20 square metres.
The play area takes 6 × 6 = 36 square metres.
The remaining area is 416 - 20 - 36 = 360 square metres.
Regular coverage needs 360 / 10 = 36 roll equivalents.
Allowing extra needs 36 + 36 × 10 / 100 = 39.6 roll equivalents.
After existing stock, 39.6 - 4 = 35.6 roll equivalents are missing.
That exceeds the coverage of 35 rolls, so buy 35 + 1 = 36 rolls.
answer: The group should buy 36 whole rolls.

user: The makers at a Patan workshop earn 35 rupees per notebook. Kavya starts with a two-hour solo stint at 18 notebooks per hour. A second maker joins at 22 per hour, and they work together for 90 minutes. The next day they sell every notebook at that price and pay 11 rupees each for materials and a flat 300-rupee stall fee. What stays with the workshop?
think:
The solo stint provides 2 × 18 = 36 notebooks.
Their combined rate is 18 + 22 = 40 notebooks an hour.
The shared time is 90 / 60 = 1.5 hours.
The pair adds 1.5 × 40 = 60 notebooks.
The full sale count is 36 + 60 = 96.
Each sale leaves 35 - 11 = 24 rupees after materials.
After rent the workshop retains 96 × 24 - 300 = 2004 rupees.

user: A music teacher in Alwar bought 80 matching bells. She returned 12 faulty bells at their full price of 30 rupees each. Of the good bells, she gives 8 away and sells the others at 55 rupees each. An assistant earns a commission of 5% of the sales. Once the refund, sales and commission are all included, how much more money does she have than before the original purchase?
think:
Buying the batch costs 80 × 30 = 2400 rupees.
The faulty items bring back 12 × 30 = 360 rupees.
The number sold is 80 - 12 - 8 = 60 bells.
Gross sales are 60 × 55 = 3300 rupees.
The commission is 3300 × 5 / 100 = 165 rupees.
Her cash gain is 360 + 3300 - 2400 - 165 = 1095 rupees.
answer: She has 1095 rupees more than before the purchase.

user: In Durgapur a shuttle operator charges 140 rupees for the first 8 km, then 13 rupees per km for the next 12 km and 18 rupees per km beyond that. On a 27 km trip there is a 52-rupee toll. The fare alone is discounted by 10%. A client pays 100 rupees upfront towards the bill. What balance is due?
think:
The highest rate applies to 27 - 8 - 12 = 7 km.
The intermediate charge is 12 × 13 = 156 rupees.
The final band adds 7 × 18 = 126 rupees.
The eligible fare is 140 + 156 + 126 = 422 rupees.
The reduction is 422 × 10 / 100 = 42.2 rupees.
The final bill with toll is 422 - 42.2 + 52 = 431.8 rupees.
The advance brings the balance to 431.8 - 100 = 331.8 rupees.
answer: The client owes 331 rupees and 80 paise.

user: A Rajahmundry nursery buys 180 seedlings, discards 15 damaged ones and donates one-fifth of the healthy ones. The rest must be set out in six equal rows. Each row has 5 markers already, and the nursery wants one marker for each seedling. It buys markers in strips of 8. How many strips are needed, and how many bought markers will be spare?
think:
The healthy count is 180 - 15 = 165 seedlings.
The donation uses 165 / 5 = 33 seedlings.
The nursery keeps 165 - 33 = 132 seedlings.
Each row therefore takes 132 / 6 = 22 seedlings.
Existing markers leave 22 - 5 = 17 needed per row.
All six rows need 6 × 17 = 102 new markers.
Twelve strips supply 12 × 8 = 96, so one more is needed.
The spare count with 13 strips is 13 × 8 - 102 = 2.
answer: Buy 13 strips. There will be 2 spare markers.
